candidates.label: Persentase penduduk miskin
candidates.institution: Badan Pusat Statistik Provinsi Jawa Barat
candidates.coverage: All 27 Jawa Barat kabupaten/kota: 18 kabupaten (3201–3218) and nine kota (3271–3279); 27 actual 2023 values inspected, with kabupaten and kota kept distinct.
candidates.definition: Share of persons whose monthly per-capita expenditure falls below the local BPS food and non-food poverty line. Source already publishes the percentage; do not divide poor-person counts by a different population projection.
candidates.reason: All 27 existing v1 percentages independently matched to table 4.6.2. Higher poverty denotes greater basic-needs deprivation; no scoring applied.
limitations: Regional aggregates do not identify within-region inequality; no missing values filled or imputed.
Table 4.6.2 labels 2023 only; March reference is corroborated by the chapter narrative, not printed in every district row.
Susenas survey estimates have sampling uncertainty; yearbook does not provide district standard errors here.
Local poverty lines differ with local consumption needs and prices.

candidates.label: Tingkat Pengangguran Terbuka (TPT)
candidates.institution: Badan Pusat Statistik Provinsi Jawa Barat
candidates.coverage: All 27 Jawa Barat kabupaten/kota: 18 kabupaten (3201–3218) and nine kota (3271–3279); 27 actual 2023 values inspected, with kabupaten and kota kept distinct.
candidates.definition: Unemployed persons as a percentage of the labour force aged 15 years and over, from August 2023 Sakernas. Denominator is economically active persons, not all residents.
candidates.reason: All 27 existing v1 TPT values independently matched to table 3.2.16, 2023 TPT column. Higher TPT denotes greater open-unemployment burden; no scoring applied.
limitations: Regional aggregates do not identify within-region inequality; no missing values filled or imputed.
TPT excludes people outside the labour force; low TPT does not prove adequate employment, wages, hours, or job quality.
2023 TPT uses SP2020 population-projection weights; do not mix alternative survey waves or weights.
District survey standard errors are not supplied in this table.

candidates.label: Akses rumah tangga terhadap sanitasi layak
candidates.institution: Badan Pusat Statistik Provinsi Jawa Barat
candidates.coverage: All 27 Jawa Barat kabupaten/kota: 18 kabupaten (3201–3218) and nine kota (3271–3279); 27 actual 2023 values inspected, with kabupaten and kota kept distinct.
candidates.definition: Percentage of households with improved sanitation, not safely managed sanitation. Contemporary 2023 Susenas methodological notes define own/shared/communal facilities, goose-neck toilets, and septic tank or wastewater treatment; rural earth pits are also included under the 2019 national concept.
candidates.reason: All 27 existing v1 values independently matched to table 4.3.8. Lower improved-sanitation coverage indicates greater household-service shortfall; no scoring applied.
limitations: Regional aggregates do not identify within-region inequality; no missing values filled or imputed.
Household share, not population share; English yearbook title says household population, while Indonesian title explicitly identifies rumah tangga.
Yearbook table identifies Susenas and year only, without district sampling errors or the full operational rule.
Operational rule cross-checked in BPS Jawa Timur 2023 Susenas methodology, a national-concept explanation rather than an independent Jawa Barat observation source.
Improved sanitation does not establish safe containment, desludging, treatment, or compliance with safely managed sanitation.
evidence: https://jabar.bps.go.id/id/publication/2024/02/28/35ffe2d35104b39feb577e8f/provinsi-jawa-barat-dalam-angka-2024.html — 4.3.8; printed 261 / PDF 337, 2023 column (6), Susenas source

candidates.label: Akses rumah tangga terhadap sumber air minum layak
candidates.institution: Badan Pusat Statistik Provinsi Jawa Barat
candidates.coverage: All 27 Jawa Barat kabupaten/kota: 18 kabupaten (3201–3218) and nine kota (3271–3279); 27 actual 2023 values inspected, with kabupaten and kota kept distinct.
candidates.definition: Percentage of households with access to an improved drinking-water source. Contemporary 2023 Susenas notes identify piped/protected water; bottled/refill-water households qualify when their bathing/washing source is also improved. This is improved-source access, not laboratory-tested drinking-water safety.
candidates.reason: All 27 official 2023 values transcribed from table 4.3.9, 2023 column (5). Lower improved-source coverage indicates greater basic-service shortfall; no scoring applied.
limitations: Regional aggregates do not identify within-region inequality; no missing values filled or imputed.
Households are the denominator, not persons, piped-water customers, or water-service connections.
Yearbook table labels 2023 Susenas only; no within-year survey date or standard errors are given in this table.
Operational rule cross-checked in contemporary BPS Jawa Timur 2023 Susenas methodology under the national 2019 Bappenas concept; that publication supplies definitions only, not Jawa Barat values.
Do not apply the older SIRUSA indicator 1002615 (created 2015, associated activity 2002), which explicitly excludes bottled water and differs from the contemporary 2023 operational concept.
Improved-source access does not establish safe quality, reliability, affordability, travel time, or safely managed water.
evidence: https://jabar.bps.go.id/id/publication/2024/02/28/35ffe2d35104b39feb577e8f/provinsi-jawa-barat-dalam-angka-2024.html — 4.3.9; printed 262 / PDF 338, 2023 column (5); 18 kabupaten then nine kota; Susenas source

candidates.label: Jumlah Puskesmas
candidates.institution: Dinas Kesehatan Provinsi Jawa Barat, reproduced by Badan Pusat Statistik Provinsi Jawa Barat
candidates.coverage: All 27 Jawa Barat kabupaten/kota: 18 kabupaten (3201–3218) and nine kota (3271–3279); 27 actual 2023 values inspected, with kabupaten and kota kept distinct.
candidates.definition: Total Puskesmas facilities, with and without inpatient care, as published for 2023. Excludes Puskesmas pembantu, mobile units, private primary clinics, Posyandu, and hospitals.
candidates.reason: All 27 published total counts verified; sum is 1,106, matching the provincial total. Raw counts support the separately documented per-population ratio but do not measure actual access.
limitations: Regional aggregates do not identify within-region inequality; no missing values filled or imputed.
Absolute counts scale with region size and population and have no defensible standalone deprivation direction.
Exact facility inventory date is not stated.
Facility numbers do not measure staffing, opening hours, workload, distance, service quality, or utilization.
Inpatient/non-inpatient categories change in some rows; use the published total, not an assumed stable facility category.
evidence: https://jabar.bps.go.id/id/publication/2024/02/28/35ffe2d35104b39feb577e8f/provinsi-jawa-barat-dalam-angka-2024.html — 4.2.7; printed 235–237 / PDF 311–313; total 2023 column (11), PDF 312; Dinas Kesehatan source on PDF 313

candidates.label: Ketersediaan Puskesmas per 100.000 penduduk
candidates.institution: Dinas Kesehatan Provinsi Jawa Barat, reproduced by Badan Pusat Statistik Provinsi Jawa Barat
candidates.coverage: All 27 Jawa Barat kabupaten/kota: 18 kabupaten (3201–3218) and nine kota (3271–3279); 27 actual 2023 values inspected, with kabupaten and kota kept distinct.
candidates.definition: Derived facility availability: published 2023 total Puskesmas count / 2023 population in exact persons from health-profile appendix table 1 * 100000. Population counts match the SP2020-based yearbook projection series rounded to 0.01 thousand.
candidates.reason: Both numerator and denominator have all 27 regions and year 2023. Every derived row identifies the exact denominator and source. Keep as context: facility availability is not observed primary-healthcare access, and a single deprivation direction ignores catchment geography and other providers.
limitations: Regional aggregates do not identify within-region inequality; no missing values filled or imputed.
This transparent derived ratio is not a claim to reproduce the health profile narrative ratio, which uses conflicting population figures.

Health-profile table 1 population source names BPS and Kementerian Kesehatan; yearbook identifies the corroborating 2020–2035 SP2020 projection series. No exact within-year date is supplied in the appendix.
BPS annual resident-population denominator differs conceptually from patient catchments, daytime population, and cross-boundary utilization.
Same-year count and population do not establish matched census dates.
A rural region may need more facilities per resident to meet travel-distance needs; private clinics and hospitals can substitute for urban residents.
evidence: https://jabar.bps.go.id/id/publication/2024/02/28/35ffe2d35104b39feb577e8f/provinsi-jawa-barat-dalam-angka-2024.html — 4.2.7; printed 236 / PDF 312, total 2023 column (11)

candidates.label: Angka kesakitan DBD per 100.000 penduduk
candidates.institution: Dinas Kesehatan Provinsi Jawa Barat, reproduced by Badan Pusat Statistik Provinsi Jawa Barat
candidates.coverage: All 27 Jawa Barat kabupaten/kota: 18 kabupaten (3201–3218) and nine kota (3271–3279); 27 actual 2023 values inspected, with kabupaten and kota kept distinct.
candidates.definition: Publisher-reported annual 2023 dengue haemorrhagic fever incidence per 100,000 population, taken verbatim from the explicitly labelled DBD column. Not case count, case fatality, malaria incidence, or all dengue infection prevalence.
candidates.reason: All 27 published rates exist and their units are explicit, but core comparability fails: the population base cannot be reconciled with official 2023 cases and available population counts. Preserve rates only as published context; do not compute or score a replacement rate.
limitations: Regional aggregates do not identify within-region inequality; no missing values filled or imputed.
Bogor: health-profile table 72 reports 1,881 cases, while table 1 reports 5,627,021 people. Their ratio gives 33.42798969472479 per 100,000, not the published 31.
Province: 19,328 cases / 49,860,330 people * 100000 = 38.76428415134838, not the published 38; do not infer an unreported population base or rounding rule.
Health-profile narrative figure I.1 uses different district population counts than its appendix table 1; even narrative district populations do not reconcile all published rates.
Disease surveillance reflects diagnosis and reporting as well as transmission; stronger case detection can raise recorded incidence.
Higher published incidence describes disease burden, not necessarily worse municipal governance or weaker healthcare.
Units are not ambiguous here, but population-vintage/denominator comparability remains unresolved. No core classification and no imputation.
evidence: https://jabar.bps.go.id/id/publication/2024/02/28/35ffe2d35104b39feb577e8f/provinsi-jawa-barat-dalam-angka-2024.html — 4.2.6; printed 233–234 / PDF 309–310; DBD column (7) explicitly per 100,000 population

candidates.label: Penduduk sebagai penyebut dan konteks
candidates.institution: Badan Pusat Statistik Provinsi Jawa Barat; exact counts reproduced in Dinas Kesehatan appendix
candidates.coverage: All 27 Jawa Barat kabupaten/kota: 18 kabupaten (3201–3218) and nine kota (3271–3279); 27 actual 2023 values inspected, with kabupaten and kota kept distinct.
candidates.definition: 2023 resident population in exact persons from health-profile appendix table 1. The 27 counts match the yearbook table 3.1.1 SP2020-based Jawa Barat population projections 2020–2035 when expressed in the yearbook unit of 0.01 thousand persons.
candidates.reason: All 27 exact counts acquired; total is 49,860,330. Retain this explicit projection-series denominator for Puskesmas availability. Population size alone is neither civic deprivation nor advantage.

The appendix does not state the exact within-year reference date; do not label June or December without further evidence.
This denominator cannot be assumed to underlie DBD incidence, poverty estimates, TPT, or household access percentages.

candidates.label: Kepadatan penduduk
candidates.institution: Badan Pusat Statistik Provinsi Jawa Barat
candidates.coverage: All 27 Jawa Barat kabupaten/kota: 18 kabupaten (3201–3218) and nine kota (3271–3279); 27 actual 2023 values inspected, with kabupaten and kota kept distinct.
candidates.definition: Official 2023 population density per square kilometre, using yearbook population projections and administrative areas under Kepmendagri 100.1.1-6117 Tahun 2022. The superscript 5 after km in the PDF header is an area-basis footnote, not a fifth-power unit.
candidates.reason: All 27 published 2023 densities acquired directly. Keep as settlement context: high density can support efficient services and create congestion or exposure; no single deprivation direction is defensible.
limitations: Regional aggregates do not identify within-region inequality; no missing values filled or imputed.
Use the yearbook administrative-area version consistently. Health-profile appendix densities use different area figures and must not be merged.
Density is an administrative-region average, not built-up-area crowding or household overcrowding.
Population is projected; units and boundaries differ from alternative density releases.
